pred_ddx.label: Intraductal Carcinoma of the Breast (in situ component)

Invasive Adenocarcinoma of the Breast: The patient has a mass in the upper outer quadrant of her left breast, elevated Ca 15-3 levels, and invasive carcinoma was found on excisional biopsy. Microscopic examination showed average-sized cells with well-defined borders and polygonal contours, and the tumor is positive for estrogen receptors (ER). These findings are consistent with invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast.

The patient's breast mass was found to be an invasive carcinoma on excisional biopsy, with microscopic examination showing average-sized cells with well-defined borders and polygonal contours, and positive for estrogen receptors (ER) and negative for progesterone receptors (PgR). The mass was also lobulated and well-defined on mammogram, and hypoechoic and well-circumscribed on ultrasound, with elevated Ca 15-3 levels.
Intraductal Carcinoma of the Breast (in: The patient's biopsy showed a few ducts with an intraductal (in situ) carcinoma of solid type, with no lymphovascular invasion, and positive for keratins AE1/AE3, EMA and Cytokeratin 7 on histochemical examination.
